title: Peony Blush — Spring Countryside Bridal Cover
description: A watercolor-washed wedding cover built around an illustrated peony-and-eucalyptus crown, flowing script names as the hero element, and a delicate italic date beneath — the visual language of fine bridal stationery translated to a single opening slide.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment a presentation stops being a document and becomes a keepsake. It refuses hard edges, geometric grids, and high-contrast corporate polish in favor of painterly washes and hand-lettered warmth. It is designed for speakers who want their opening slide to feel like the inside cover of a gilded journal, not a boardroom deck. The audience it serves has already bought into the emotion of the occasion — the slide's only job is to honor that.
goodFor: Wedding ceremony or reception welcome slides
Spring seasonal event openers built around a single illustrated motif
avoidFor: Tech product launches or SaaS investor pitch decks
Dark-room rear-projection conference setups where pastels wash out
Multi-column data tables or dense infographic layouts
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the opening page of a hand-bound bridal journal — tender, still, and suffused with soft spring light filtering through gauze. A painterly floral crown drifts above a flowing script centerpiece, the whole composition held together by generous breathing room rather than structural containment. Mood is ceremonial quietude: romantic, unhurried, and intimate. Avoid all hard geometry, drop shadows, structured grids, or any element that would interrupt the watercolor illusion of something made by hand.

examples.layoutNotes: Single centered column occupying roughly the middle 60% of slide width; the illustrated peony-and-eucalyptus crown anchors the upper third, its watercolor wash bleeding softly toward the top edge with no hard crop. Script hero text — couple's names or event title — sits at the vertical midpoint as the dominant compositional element. An italic date or subtitle follows one clear step below, separated by negative space alone or a thin hand-drawn flourish, never a rule line. Wide outer margins on all four sides; no footer band, no header strip, no bounding boxes of any kind.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like an interior spread of fine bridal stationery — intimate, hand-crafted, and unhurried. A small watercolor botanical cluster anchoring one corner provides asymmetric warmth while the content area breathes with generous surrounding whitespace. Avoid tabular structure, bullet-list rigidity, or hard geometric borders; let spacing and a single decorative flourish carry all organizational work. The mood is tender and keepsake-quality — as though this page could be pressed into the wedding album alongside the invitation suite.
